chunks: And he who narrated it: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Umar ibn Aban, who said:

I arrived at the door of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so al-Mufaddal came out and I faced him. He said to me, 'What is the matter with you?' I said, 'I intend to do something, but I have not done it until Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) commands me. I intend that Allah should guard my private part and lower my gaze during my ihram.' He said to me, 'As you are,' and entered. He asked him about that, and he said, 'This al-Kalbi is at the door, and he intends to enter ihram and intends to marry, so that Allah should lower his gaze thereby. If you command him, he will do it, and if not, he will turn away from that.'
So he said to me, 'Command him to do it and let him conceal himself.'

His saying (peace be upon him) 'let him do it' means before he enters into ihram. As for after he enters into it, it is not permissible for him to do that, according to what we have previously mentioned. If the muhrim contracts the marriage while he is aware of the prohibition of that, they are separated, and she is not permissible for him ever. He narrated that.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ihram, the state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْكَلْبِيُّ: Al-Kalbi (a specific person mentioned in the narration)

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim contract a marriage while in the state of ihram, and what is the ruling if he does so knowingly?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Imam’s pragmatic approach to preventing *zina* by permitting marriage during *ihram*, specifically noting the distinction between contracting the marriage before or during the state of consecration. Scholarly commentary clarifies that while the marriage is valid, if performed while aware of the prohibition, it results in permanent separation (*takhliyah*) rather than temporary divorce, emphasizing the gravity of violating *ihram* conditions. This ruling highlights the balance between preserving chastity and maintaining the sanctity of the pilgrimage rites.
